speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you describe exactly what happens during these episodes of unresponsiveness, and how long they typically last? Also, do you have any awareness of the facial grimacing while it is occurring?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes lasting 3–4 minutes each of facial grimacing and staring over the past month. During these episodes, he is nonresponsive and does not recall them afterward. He reports a muddy taste in his mouth before the onset of these episodes. His brother witnessed him waking up, staring, and making hand gestures during one episode. The patient felt lethargic and confused afterwards.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the patient have a history of febrile seizures, and have you noticed any triggers like sleep deprivation or stress? REQUEST TEST: EEG

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Electroencephalogram: Interictal spikes and sharp waves localized to the temporal lobes, more prominent on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any history of head trauma or neurological infections? Do you notice any sensory symptoms, such as visual disturbances or smells, before the episodes begin?

speaker: Doctor
text: The muddy taste serves as an aura, and the EEG findings strongly point to focal seizures originating in the right temporal lobe. To rule out a structural cause for these seizures, I need to visualize the brain's anatomy. REQUEST TEST: MRI Brain

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: MRI Brain: No evidence of mass lesions, infarctions, or structural abnormalities.

speaker: Doctor
text: The MRI is normal, ruling out structural causes like tumors or scars. Given the classic aura, post-ictal confusion, and right temporal EEG findings, the diagnosis is clear. DIAGNOSIS READY: Right temporal lobe epilepsy
